candidates.obligation_text: A data controller or data processor shall bear the burden of proof for establishing a data subject's consent to the processing of their personal data for a specified purpose.

candidates.source_section: Section 33(2), Data Protection Act 2019 (Processing of personal data relating to a child)
candidates.object: appropriate mechanisms for age verification and consent
candidates.obligation_text: A data controller or data processor shall incorporate appropriate mechanisms for age verification and consent in order to process personal data of a child.

candidates.obligation_text: The data controller or data processor shall implement mechanisms to ensure that time limits established for the rectification, erasure or restriction of processing of personal data, or for a periodic review of the need for the storage of the personal data, is observed.

candidates.source_section: Section 39(1), Data Protection Act 2019 (Limitation to retention of personal data)
candidates.obligation_text: A data controller or data processor shall retain personal data only as long as may be reasonably necessary to satisfy the purpose for which it is processed unless the retention is — (a) required or authorised by law; (b) reasonably necessary for a lawful purpose; (c) authorised or consented by the data subject; or (d) for historical, statistical, journalistic literature and art or research purposes.

candidates.obligation_text: A data controller or data processor shall delete, erase, anonymise or pseudonymise personal data not necessary to be retained under sub-section (1) in a manner as may be specified at the expiry of the retention period.

candidates.obligation_text: The withdrawal of consent under sub-section (2) shall not affect the lawfulness of processing based on prior consent before its withdrawal.

candidates.source_section: Section 32(4), Data Protection Act 2019 (Conditions for consent)
candidates.obligation_text: In determining whether consent was freely given, account shall be taken of whether, among others, the performance of a contract, including the provision of a service, is conditional on consent to the processing of personal data that is not necessary for the performance of that contract.

candidates.condition: Where the data controller has shared the personal data with a third party for processing purposes, the data controller or data processor shall take all reasonable steps to inform third parties processing such data, that the data subject has requested
candidates.obligation_text: Where the data controller has shared the personal data with a third party for processing purposes, the data controller or data processor shall take all reasonable steps to inform third parties processing such data, that the data subject has requested — (a) the rectification of such personal data in their possession or under their control that is inaccurate, out-dated, incomplete or misleading; or (b) the erasure or destruction of such personal data that the data controller is no longer authorised to retain, irrelevant, excessive or obtained unlawfully.

candidates.source_section: Section 49(1), Data Protection Act 2019 (Safeguards prior to transfer of personal data out of Kenya)
candidates.obligation_text: The out of Kenya shall only be effected upon obtaining consent of a data subject and on obtaining confirmation of appropriate safeguards.

candidates.condition: Where processing of personal data is restricted under this section
candidates.obligation_text: Where processing of personal data is restricted under this section— (a) the personal data shall, unless the data is being stored, only be processed with the data subject's consent or for the establishment, exercise or defence of a legal claim, the protection of the rights of another person or for reasons of public interest; and (b) the data controller shall inform the data subject before withdrawing the of the personal data.

candidates.obligation_text: A person shall not use, for commercial purposes, personal data obtained pursuant to the provisions of this Act unless the person — (a) has sought and obtained express consent from a data subject; or (b) is authorised to do so under any written law and the data subject has been informed of such use when collecting the data from the data subject.
